claims.claim: Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple on earth
claims.quote: Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world, and ranks with Bagan in Myanmar and Angkor Wat in Cambodia as one of the great archeological sites of Southeast Asia.

claims.claim: The temple consists of nine stacked stone platforms
claims.quote: the temple consists of nine stacked platforms, six square and three circular, topped by a central dome

claims.claim: It has 2,672 relief panels and originally 504 Buddha statues
claims.quote: It is decorated with 2,672 relief panels and originally 504 Buddha statues.

claims.claim: The monument lay under volcanic ash and jungle growth for centuries
claims.quote: Borobudur lay hidden for centuries under layers of volcanic ash and jungle growth.

claims.claim: The aerial image is a panoramic view of Borobudur dated 2006, CC0
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Panoramic views of Borobudur.jpg ... Date: 2006-03-13 19:17:25 ... Licence: CC0

claims.claim: In 1896 King Chulalongkorn of Siam was allowed to take home eight cartloads of sculpture from Borobudur
claims.quote: In 1896 King Chulalongkorn of Siam visited Java and requested and was allowed to take home eight cartloads of sculptures taken from Borobudur.

claims.claim: The removed material included thirty relief pieces, five Buddha images, two lions and a guardian statue
claims.quote: These include thirty pieces taken from a number of relief panels, five buddha images, two lions, one gargoyle, several kala motifs from the stairs and gateways, and a guardian statue (dvarapala).

claims.claim: The 1896 photograph comes from King Chulalongkorn's Java diary of 1896
claims.quote: Borobudur (undated), a photograph from the book "Diary of King Chulalongkorn's 1901 Trip to Java". Likely an image from his 1896 trip

claims.claim: There are 1,460 narrative relief panels
claims.quote: The monument guides pilgrims through an extensive system of stairways and corridors with 1,460 narrative relief panels on the walls and the balustrades.

claims.claim: The narrative reliefs extend about three kilometres
claims.quote: The narrative reliefs are arranged into 11 series over a length of 3,000 metres (9,800 ft) around the hidden foot and the first four galleries of the monument.

claims.claim: Panels on the walls read right to left, while those on the balustrades read left to right
claims.quote: Narrative panels on the wall read from right to left, while those on the balustrade read from left to right.

claims.claim: This reading order follows the pilgrim's clockwise circumambulation of the monument
claims.quote: This conforms with pradaksina, the ritual of circumambulation performed by pilgrims who move in a clockwise direction while keeping the sanctuary to their right.

claims.claim: The gallery photograph is by O. Kurkdjian and dates to c. 1900
claims.quote: Vervaardiger:  fotograaf: O. Kurkdjian ... Datering:  ca. 1895 - ca. 1915

claims.claim: The gallery photograph is by O. Kurkdjian, c. 1895–1915, Rijksmuseum
claims.quote: Vervaardiger:  fotograaf: O. Kurkdjian ... Datering:  ca. 1895 - ca. 1915

claims.claim: Of the 504 Buddha statues, 43 are missing
claims.quote: Of the original 504 buddha statues, over 300 are damaged (mostly headless), and 43 are missing.

claims.claim: Over 300 of the Buddha statues are damaged, mostly headless
claims.quote: Of the original 504 buddha statues, over 300 are damaged (mostly headless), and 43 are missing.

claims.claim: Buddha heads reached museums in Amsterdam, Paris and London
claims.quote: Some of these Buddha heads are now displayed in numbers of museums, such as the Tropenmuseum in Amsterdam, Musée Guimet in Paris, and The British Museum in London.

claims.claim: Germany returned its collection in 2014 and funded reattachment of the heads
claims.quote: Germany has in 2014 returned its collection and funded their reattachment and further conservation of the site.

claims.claim: The Buddha head shown is from Borobudur, dated 800–850, held by the Rijksmuseum
claims.quote: Plaats vervaardiging:   Borobudur  Datering:  800 - 850 ... Author: Rijksmuseum

claims.claim: Theodoor van Erp reconstructed the tiered parasol (chattra) pinnacle in 1911
claims.quote: The restoration was completed in 1911 and at first glance, Borobudur had been restored to its old glory. Van Erp went further by carefully reconstructing the chattra (three-tiered parasol) pinnacle on top of the main stupa.

claims.claim: Van Erp later dismantled the pinnacle because there were too few original stones, and the original design is unknown
claims.quote: However, he later dismantled the chattra, citing that there were not enough original stones used in reconstructing the pinnacle, which means that the original design of Borobudur's pinnacle is actually unknown.

claims.claim: The terrace photograph is by Frank Hurley, 1913, State Library of NSW
claims.quote: A terrace on the temple of Borobudur, Java, Indonesia, 1913, Frank Hurley, from vintage watercolour, State Library of New South Wales

claims.claim: The whole complex was fully unearthed by 1835
claims.quote: Christiaan Lodewijk Hartmann, the resident of the Kedu region, continued Cornelius's work, and in 1835, the whole complex was finally unearthed.

claims.claim: Why the monument was abandoned is unknown
claims.quote: The facts behind its abandonment remain a mystery.

claims.claim: Between 1975 and 1982 Indonesia and UNESCO dismantled over one million stones and rebuilt the monument
claims.quote: The Indonesian government and UNESCO then undertook the complete overhaul of the monument in a big restoration project between 1975 and 1982.

claims.claim: Over one million stones were dismantled and individually catalogued
claims.quote: Over one million stones were dismantled and removed during the restoration, and set aside like pieces of a massive jig-saw puzzle to be individually identified, catalogued, cleaned and treated for preservation.

claims.claim: The rebuilding included improved drainage
claims.quote: The restoration involved the dismantling of the five square platforms and the improvement of drainage by embedding water channels into the monument.

claims.claim: The date of abandonment is still unknown
claims.quote: It is not known when active use of the monument and Buddhist pilgrimage to it ceased.

claims.claim: The 1973 photograph is from the Government of Indonesia
claims.quote: Date: 1973-08-10 Author: Photo owner: Government of Republic of Indonesia

claims.claim: Borobudur is a 9th-century temple in Central Java
claims.quote: Borobudur ... is a 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in Magelang Regency, near the town of Muntilan, northwest of the city of Yogyakarta, in Central Java, Indonesia.

claims.claim: There are no records of Borobudur's construction or its intended purpose
claims.quote: There are no known records of construction or the intended purpose of Borobudur.

claims.claim: In 1814 Stamford Raffles, then British ruler of Java, was told by local people about a big monument in the jungle near Bumisegoro
claims.quote: On an inspection tour to Semarang in 1814, he was informed about a big monument deep in a jungle near the village of Bumisegoro.

claims.claim: Raffles sent the Dutch engineer Hermann Cornelius, who with 200 men spent two months cutting trees, burning vegetation and digging away earth
claims.quote: In two months, Cornelius and his 200 men cut down trees, burned down vegetation and dug away the earth to reveal the monument.

claims.claim: Raffles never visited the site but is still credited with the rediscovery
claims.quote: Although Raffles mentioned the discovery in only a few sentences in his book, and did not visit the site himself, he has been credited with the monument's rediscovery, as the one who had brought it to the world's attention.

claims.claim: Parts of the temple were taken as souvenirs, some with colonial-government consent
claims.quote: Borobudur was considered as the source of souvenirs, and parts of its sculptures were looted, some even with colonial-government consent.

claims.claim: Borobudur became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991
claims.quote: After the renovation was finished, UNESCO listed Borobudur as a World Heritage Site in 1991.

claims.claim: A capital move after volcanic eruptions sometime between 928 and 1006 is the most likely period of abandonment
claims.quote: Sometime between 928 and 1006, King Mpu Sindok moved the capital of the Mataram kingdom to the region of East Java after a series of volcanic eruptions; it is not certain whether this influenced the abandonment, but several sources mention this as the most likely period of abandonment.
